questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the following as used in Internet communication:

(a) URL. (1 mark)

(b) HTTPs. (2 marks)

(c) VoIP. (1 mark)

(d) Telnet. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) URL (1 mark)**

The **Uniform Resource Locator** is the **unique address of a resource** (a web page, an image, a file) on the Internet. It is made of the protocol, the domain name and the path, for example `https://www.example.com/folder/page.html`.

**(b) HTTPS (2 marks)**

**HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure** is the version of HTTP in which the data exchanged between the browser and the web server are **encrypted with SSL/TLS**; the server is **authenticated by a digital certificate**, so the data cannot be read or changed on the way (the browser shows a padlock). It is used for online banking, shopping and login pages.

**(c) VoIP (1 mark)**

**Voice over Internet Protocol** is the technology that **converts speech into digital packets and sends them over the Internet (or any IP network)**, so that **telephone calls are made through the Internet** instead of the public telephone network (for example Skype, WhatsApp calls).

**(d) Telnet (1 mark)**

Telnet is a protocol and program that lets a user **log in to a remote computer over a network and control it with text commands** as if sitting at it. It sends everything unencrypted, which is why it has been replaced by the secure SSH.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is software End User License Agreement? (2 marks)

(b) Differentiate between open source and freeware. (2 marks)

(c) Give TWO ways that the author's right can be protected for software. (2 marks)

(d) Give TWO ways that software piracy can be controlled. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) End User License Agreement (EULA) (2 marks)**

It is a **legal contract between the owner (publisher) of the software and the user**. It states **what the user may do** (for example how many computers it can be installed on) and **what is forbidden** (copying and selling it, modifying it, reverse engineering), and it limits the publisher's liability. The user **accepts it ("I agree") when installing** the software.

**(b) Open source and freeware (2 marks)**

- **Open-source software**: the **source code is made available**, so users may **study, modify and redistribute** it (under a licence such as the GPL); it is often free but not necessarily (Linux, LibreOffice).
- **Freeware**: the program is **free to use but the source code is not available**; the author keeps the copyright, and the user **cannot modify or redistribute it** except as the licence allows (for example Adobe Reader).

**(c) Two ways to protect the author's right (2 marks)**

- **Copyright law and notice**: the work is protected by copyright (the © notice), and **licence agreements (EULA)** set the conditions of use; legal action can be taken against offenders.
- **Technical protection**: **product keys / activation codes**, hardware keys (dongles), **digital rights management (DRM)**, encryption, and **patents** for inventions.

**(d) Two ways to control software piracy (2 marks)**

- **Product activation and licence keys**, with online checking, so that a copy cannot be installed on unlimited computers; **dongles** and DRM.
- **Laws and penalties** enforced by the police and courts, **software audits** in organisations, and **education/awareness** of users; also selling **cheaper licences**, or **site/volume licences** and using open-source software, which reduce the temptation to copy.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the function of the following in a computer system:

(a) ROM. (1 mark)

(b) Register. (1 mark)

(c) Ports. (1 mark)

(d) Accumulator (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) ROM (1 mark)**

**Read-only memory** is **non-volatile** memory whose contents are not lost when the power is switched off. It **stores the start-up (boot) program / BIOS and firmware** that the computer needs to begin working.

**(b) Register (1 mark)**

A register is a **very small, very fast storage location inside the CPU** that **temporarily holds the data, instruction or address being processed** (for example the program counter, MAR, MDR, instruction register).

**(c) Ports (1 mark)**

Ports are the **sockets (interfaces) on the computer through which peripheral devices are connected** (keyboard, mouse, printer, monitor, USB storage, network cable) so that **data can pass between the computer and the device**.

**(d) Accumulator (1 mark)**

The accumulator is a **register in the ALU** that **holds the data being worked on and stores the intermediate and final results of arithmetic and logic operations**.
